newsitem.title: SPAIN: CYCLING-SVORADA TAKES ADVANTAGE OF SPRINT FINISH CRASH.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-SVORADA TAKES ADVANTAGE OF SPRINT FINISH CRASH.

text.p: Slovak Jan Svorada took advantage of a crash in the final sprint to win the second stage of the Tour of Catalonia on Friday.
But Britain's Chris Boardman, winner of Thursday's time trial, maintained his 12-second overall lead.

Svorada swept to the front of the pack after spotting a gap created by a crash in which Australian Stuart O'Grady appeared to hit a piece of fencing and brought down Ukrainian Sergei Outschakov and Spaniard Angel Edo.
O'Grady was taken to hospital but he was not seriously injured.
Earlier, Jose Daniel Bernal had built a seven-minute lead after breaking away just four kilometres into the 164-km stage between Port Aventura and Lleida.
But the Spaniard never looked likely to hang on and was hauled in 35 kms from the finish.
Saturday's 187-km stage between Las Borjas Blancas and Manresa includes a tough mountain section through Montserrat.
